answer: Graduated reputation inheritance stops Sybils in four steps. First, a retiring agent may pass standing to one successor, never a fleet. Second, only a quarter moves, after sixty days of joint signed jobs. Third, the successor earns the rest through verified work, so a bought shell stays weak. Fourth, fraud voids the transfer and burns a $40 bond. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 donors, 60,000 jobs, and $40,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust rises like a terrace above a tide, not a copied ember, like a shop passed to one apprentice proving himself daily.
